reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.
commonErrors: Using a GCS obtained after sedation.
Using a later CT instead of the initial scan.
Applying to traumatic or tumour-related haemorrhage.
name: ICH Score

version.label: ICH Score (Hemphill et al. 2001)
version.detail: Five components, 0–6. Mortality figures are observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort.

purpose: Standardised grading of spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage severity at presentation.
intendedPopulation: Adults with spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage, at presentation.

calculatorNotice.title: Severity grade, not an individual prognosis
calculatorNotice.message: Mortality figures come from a 2001 cohort with frequent early care limitation. Decisions about goals of care should not rest on this score alone.

resultStates.label: Score 0
resultStates.summary: ICH Score 0 at this assessment: 0% observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort.
resultStates.detail: Group-level figure from a small cohort; not an individual prognosis.

resultStates.label: Score 1
resultStates.summary: Observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort: 13%.

resultStates.summary: Observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort: 26%.

resultStates.label: Score 3
resultStates.summary: Observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort: 72%.
resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full clinical picture; early care limitation can make scores self-fulfilling.

resultStates.label: Score 4
resultStates.summary: Observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort: 97%.
resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full clinical picture; goals of care should not be based on the score alone.

resultStates.label: Score 5
resultStates.summary: Observed 30-day mortality in the derivation cohort: 100%.
resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full clinical picture; goals of care should not be based on the score alone.

resultStates.label: Score 6

resultStates.detail: Integrate with the full clinical picture; goals of care should not be based on the score alone.

clinicalContext.text: Describes ICH severity at presentation in a common language.

clinicalInsights.text: Early do-not-resuscitate decisions were common in the derivation era and can make prognostic scores self-fulfilling.
Guidelines advise against early care limitation based on a single prognostic score.

limitations.text: Derived in a small single-centre cohort.

limitations: Does not include haematoma expansion, anticoagulation or detailed location.
Not designed to guide individual treatment.

confounders.effect: ABC/2 can over- or under-estimate irregular haematomas.

guideSections.what: A 0–6 grading scale combining GCS, haematoma volume, intraventricular extension, infratentorial origin and age.
guideSections.whenToUse: Standardised description of ICH severity at presentation.
guideSections.howToPerform: Use the presentation GCS and initial CT. Assign points and sum.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A severity descriptor; prognostic discussions integrate the whole clinical picture.

sources.citation: Hemphill JC 3rd, Bonovich DC, Besmertis L, Manley GT, Johnston SC. The ICH score: a simple, reliable grading scale for intracerebral hemorrhage. Stroke. 2001;32(4):891-897.
